reason: Recommend the tiled NEON transpose first: it changes only the timed A conversion in the already-tested TB path, so it directly tests whether that conversion can be cheaper. The TB path’s poor scores do not isolate transpose cost or predict this result. TA adds a timed B transpose while retaining B packing and adding A packing, so its full-call cost is uncertain and its correctness mapping carries more risk. Half-band packing and 288-byte scratch stride are distinct changes, but the former adds packing and changes traversal, while the latter follows an unpromoted padded-scratch trial with no established cache cause. The four-step unroll extends an unpromoted two-step trial; the proposed K-pair schedule may alias that trial unless its instruction schedule differs. Fused transpose recomputes A’s transpose across 16 column panels, making it the least attractive full-call hypothesis. All advice is unverified; none establishes a gain.
